name: St. Louis
operatingHours: MetroLink Red and Blue Lines run ~4:00 AM–~1:00 AM daily, every ~12–15 min by day and ~20–30 min evenings and weekends. No overnight service.
fareInfo: $2.50 single ride; a One-Day Pass ($5) covers MetroLink and Metro buses. Buy at station vending machines (cards accepted) or in the Transit app, and validate before boarding — there are no turnstiles but fare checks are common. Children 5–12 and seniors with a permit pay half; under 5 ride free.

sights.name: Gateway Arch
sights.note: Eero Saarinen's 630-ft stainless-steel arch; tiny tram pods climb inside each leg to a windowed viewing deck, with a free westward-expansion museum underneath.
sights.hours: Museum & tram 9:00 AM–6:00 PM daily (to 8:00 PM Fri–Sat in summer); last tram 1 h before close; grounds 5 AM–11 PM

sights.name: City Museum
sights.note: A converted shoe warehouse turned into a giant climbable playground of salvaged tunnels, slides, caves and a rooftop Ferris wheel, for kids and adults alike.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Wed–Thu & Sun, to 9:00 PM Fri–Sat; usually closed Mon–Tue

sights.name: Saint Louis Zoo
sights.note: One of America's top free zoos, spread over Forest Park with penguins, big cats, a sea-lion basin and an apes house.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–4:00 PM daily (Oct–Dec); longer hours in summer. Free entry

sights.name: Missouri Botanical Garden
sights.note: A 79-acre garden founded in 1859, famous for its geodesic Climatron rainforest dome and a large Japanese garden.

sights.name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis
sights.note: A Romanesque-Byzantine cathedral whose domes and walls hold one of the world's largest collections of mosaics.
sights.hours: 7:00 AM–5:00 PM daily; guided tours Mon–Fri 10 AM–3 PM

sights.name: Busch Stadium
sights.note: Home of the St. Louis Cardinals, with the Arch framed beyond the outfield and Ballpark Village bars next door.
sights.hours: Cardinals home games Apr–Sep; stadium tours on selected days

sights.name: Forest Park
sights.note: A 1,300-acre park bigger than Central Park, home of the 1904 World's Fair and now the zoo, art and history museums and the Muny.

sights.name: Saint Louis Art Museum
sights.note: A free art museum in the 1904 World's Fair Palace of Fine Arts, strong on German Expressionism, American art and ancient collections.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Tue–Sun, to 9:00 PM Fri; closed Mon. Free

sights.name: Saint Louis Science Center
sights.note: A hands-on science museum with a planetarium and a glass bridge over I-64 where you can clock passing cars with radar guns.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–4:30 PM Mon & Wed–Sat, 11:00 AM–4:30 PM Sun; closed Tue. Free general entry

sights.name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery
sights.note: The historic Budweiser brewery in Soulard, with red-brick 19th-century buildings, Clydesdale stables and tastings at the end of the tour.
sights.hours: Tours 11:00 AM–5:00 PM daily; biergarten to 6:00 PM

sights.name: The Fabulous Fox Theatre
sights.note: An opulent 1929 movie palace in Grand Center, restored as the city's main venue for touring Broadway shows and concerts.
sights.hours: Box office and show times vary by performance

sights.name: Missouri History Museum
sights.note: A free museum in Forest Park telling the St. Louis story, from the 1904 World's Fair to Charles Lindbergh's Spirit of St. Louis.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily, to 8:00 PM Tue. Free

sights.name: Old Courthouse
sights.note: The domed 1860s courthouse where the Dred Scott case began, reopened in 2025 after renovation with new galleries on the fight for freedom.

sights.name: Citygarden
sights.note: A free downtown sculpture park with splash fountains and works by artists like Fernand Léger and Tom Otterness.

sights.name: Soulard Farmers Market
sights.note: A bustling market hall operating since 1779, with produce, spices, butchers and street-food stalls in the old French Soulard district.

sights.name: Tower Grove Park
sights.note: A Victorian strolling park with whimsical painted pavilions, ponds and ruins, beside the Botanical Garden; Saturday farmers market in season.

sights.name: The Delmar Loop
sights.note: A lively strip of bars, music venues and diners such as Blueberry Hill, with the St. Louis Walk of Fame stars set in the sidewalk.
sights.hours: Shops and venues vary; liveliest evenings

railStations.name: Gateway Station
railStations.note: St. Louis's Amtrak and Greyhound hub (Gateway Transportation Center): Lincoln Service to Chicago (~5h 30m), Missouri River Runner to Kansas City (~5h 40m) and the Texas Eagle to Dallas/San Antonio. Civic Center MetroLink (Red and Blue) is next door.
railStations.hours: Station open ~5:00 AM–midnight. Amtrak trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: St. Louis Lambert International Airport
airports.transitNote: The MetroLink Red Line (shown on map) stops at both Lambert Airport Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 and reaches Civic Center (for Gateway Station) in ~30 min and 8th & Pine downtown in ~35 min for the standard $2.50 fare.
airports.hours: Red Line from the airport: first ~4:15 AM, last ~12:30 AM. Late arrivals need a taxi or rideshare (~25 min downtown).
